solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Youth triumphant, causing nervous affection of the larynx

explanation.surface: A young winner's gloating seems to bring on a throat complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Child-crowing is an old name for a spasm of a child's larynx that makes a crowing sound when breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a spasmodic throat disorder in infants, a nervous condition of the voice box.

clue.text: Tempo Bach varied when involving River Jordan

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the rearranged letters enclose the river abbreviation
varied means changed about, so the letters of the first two words are rearranged

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A musician plays Bach at a changed tempo while taking in the River Jordan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Jordan' looks like one place, but River is just R and Jordan is the definition: an old slang word for a chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Jordan is a dated slang term, found in Chaucer and Shakespeare, for the bedroom vessel used as a toilet.

clue.text: Mucker, I'll be shifting first to last of rich soil

indicators.note: the opening letter of the combined string is moved round to the end

parts.note: mucker is British slang for a pal
the pronoun as written, with 'll be read as 'will be'

explanation.surface: Someone tells a mate they'll be moving on, in rustic terms about soil.
explanation.walkthrough: Mucker is British slang for a friend. Join friend and I, then move the first letter to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Humic means derived from humus, the dark organic matter that makes soil fertile.

clue.text: Church reformer dominating north window

indicators.note: in a down entry, dominating means sitting on top, so the reformer comes above the next letter

parts.note: Martin Luther, leader of the Protestant Reformation

explanation.surface: A reformer looms over the north window of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: A luthern is a dormer window, which suits 'north window' as a picture but only 'window' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A luthern is an architectural term for a dormer or lucarne window set in a roof.

clue.text: Drink precedes a display of histrionics

indicators.note: precedes says the first item is placed before the second in the entry

explanation.surface: A drinker's tipple leads on to an emotional scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a drama of something means a fuss or over-the-top emotional performance.

clue.text: Classical country group — hempen homespun?

parts.note: rus is Latin for the countryside, the root of rural

explanation.surface: Reads like a description of rustic cloth from classical times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' here is the countryside, not a nation; 'Classical' points to Latin. 'Hempen homespun' is Shakespeare's phrase for rustics in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Russet was a coarse reddish-brown homespun cloth worn by country folk, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Handle fuse I inserted

indicators.note: inserted says the single letter is put inside the other word

explanation.surface: An electrician's instruction about handling a fuse once it is in.
explanation.walkthrough: Fuse looks electrical but means to join, as in welding.
explanation.definitionFit: To wield a tool is to handle it and use it with skill.

clue.text: Decorative inlay tsarina ordered and I installed

indicators.note: installed means put inside, so the single letter goes within the rearranged ones
ordered means arranged anew, so the royal word's letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An empress commissions a decorative inlay and has it fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Intarsia is wood mosaic work, a technique of inlaying patterns into furniture or panels.

clue.text: No friend of Trinitarians, and one anti converting

indicators.note: converting means changing form, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A religious opponent of the Trinity set on converting others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converting' fits the religious surface but signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Noetians followed Noetus, who denied the distinct persons of the Trinity, so they opposed Trinitarian doctrine.

clue.text: African imprisoned, denied special surrounding

indicators.note: denied means refused, so the letters for special are taken away
surrounding says the letters to drop are the ones at the outside edges of the word

parts.note: SP is a dictionary abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: An African has been locked up without any special treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters for special sit at either end of the word for imprisoned; strip them off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hutu are a people of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Caviar for Walter, a filling course?

indicators.note: filling means occupying the inside, so the article goes within the word for course

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether caviar would make a satisfying course.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter is Sir Walter Scott, whose Scots spelling of roe Chambers records.
explanation.definitionFit: Raun is a Scott spelling of rawn, fish roe, and caviar is sturgeon roe.

clue.text: Façade of temple flanked by wings recently (but no longer)

indicators.note: flanked by means having things on either side, so the wings enclose that letter

parts.note: alae is the Latin plural for wings, used in anatomy and botany

indicators.note: a facade is the front face, so only the opening letter of the building word is used

explanation.surface: A temple's front now has wings added on each side.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for winged is tempting, but the definition is the archaic sense, of late.
explanation.definitionFit: Alate is an obsolete word meaning lately, which the bracket marks as no longer current.

clue.text: Party to duck, held in the local? (4, two words)

indicators.note: held in means kept within, so the round letter for duck goes inside the pub word

parts.note: the local is British for one's neighbourhood pub
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A duck dish served at a pub party.
explanation.walkthrough: The local is the neighbourhood pub; duck is a cricketer's nought.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in on something is to share knowledge of it, just as being party to it does.

clue.text: During a sickness, starts to yawn — that's being fed sedative

indicators.note: during means within a span, so the opening letters sit inside the illness
being fed means taking something in, again putting the pair inside the illness

parts.note: mal is French for illness, as in grand mal

indicators.note: starts means beginnings, so only the opening letters of the next two words count

explanation.surface: A patient yawning through an illness is given a sedative.
explanation.definitionFit: Amytal is a trade name for amobarbital, a barbiturate used as a sedative and sleeping drug.

clue.text: Rabbit? What one may be when brought before HM?

indicators.note: brought before says the first piece is placed ahead of the royal letters

parts.note: a rabbit may well be kept as a pet

explanation.surface: A rabbit brought before the Queen wonders what it might become.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' refers back to the rabbit. The question mark marks the definition as an example: the famous rabbit of Beatrix Potter's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Rabbit is Beatrix Potter's best-known character, so Peter is a rabbit by example.

clue.text: Horsemen circling meadows — they get a good view of the action

definitions.text: they get a good view of the action

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the horsemen enclose the meadows

parts.note: ing is a northern word for a water meadow

explanation.surface: Riders circle the fields while spectators watch closely.
explanation.walkthrough: Ing, a meadow by a river, is a dialect word found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringsiders sit beside the boxing ring or circus ring, so they have front seats at the action.

clue.text: A medley

parts.note: setter's reading: just the definition, since this is the word solvers write their own clues for

explanation.walkthrough: This was the Azed competition word: the puzzle gives only a definition, and entrants submit their own clues for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused jumble of different things is a synonym for a medley.

clue.text: Nun bagging bits of unwanted rags, such as old clothes

indicators.note: bagging means pocketing, so the nun word takes those letters inside

parts.note: a vestal virgin, or by extension a nun

indicators.note: bits are small pieces, here just the opening letters of the following words

parts.note: the opening letters of both words

explanation.surface: A nun collects scraps of old cloth for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestural means relating to vesture, or clothing, so old clothes are vestural things.

clue.text: Toxic substance that's ruined dinner

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the meal's letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: Something poisonous got into the meal and spoilt it.
explanation.definitionFit: Endrin is an organochlorine insecticide, highly poisonous and now widely banned.

clue.text: One of the sciences (Greece isn't involved)

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of the country and verb are mixed up

explanation.surface: A science that, for once, the Greeks had no hand in.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads like an aside on the history of science, but it holds the fodder and its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Energetics is the branch of physics dealing with energy and its transformations.

clue.text: Man strangely swallows coin, developing tumour

indicators.note: swallows means takes inside, so the rearranged letters enclose the currency
strangely means in an odd way, so the short word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man swallows a coin and ends up with a growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuroma is a growth of nerve tissue, a type of tumour.

clue.text: Aristo's head is thus replacing contents of clean tumbril

indicators.note: the inner letters of the last word are swapped out for the new pieces

parts.note: the word whose inside is replaced

indicators.note: head means top, so only the opening letter of the aristocrat is kept

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's head in a French Revolution tumbril, ready for the guillotine.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the middle three letters of clean and put the new chunk between C and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A caisson is an ammunition wagon, and tumbril is also an old name for a military cart of that kind.

clue.text: What'll help you get a grip? As things are, tea, among group of seven? (10, two words)

definitions.text: What'll help you get a grip?

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the first two pieces go inside the group of seven

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone advised to get a grip is offered tea among a group of seven.
explanation.walkthrough: The seven deadly sins are the group of seven; cha (char) is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chains fitted round car tyres give traction on snowy roads, literally helping wheels grip.

clue.text: Smoked sausage that is following tiny starter of niçoise

indicators.note: following says the abbreviation for that is comes after the other pieces
the starter is the first course, so just the opening letter of the French dish word

explanation.surface: A smoked sausage served after a small salad niçoise starter.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter plays on the meal course but just means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A weenie is North American slang for a frankfurter or wiener, a smoked sausage.

clue.text: Revolutionary group around active Red

indicators.note: active means stirring and busy, so the colour word's letters move about

parts.note: ca is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A revolutionary cell gathers round an active Communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal, but it is circa abbreviated, simply placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group of trained activists, especially within a Communist revolutionary party.

clue.text: Connect knot for legging

parts.note: as a telephone operator puts a caller through

explanation.surface: An instruction to tie a knot to secure a legging.
explanation.definitionFit: Puttie is a variant spelling of puttee, a cloth strip wound round the lower leg as a legging.

clue.text: Cheers enveloping fringe subject

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping round, so the thanks word goes around the edge word

explanation.surface: A toast at an event about some fringe subject.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers is British for thanks here, not a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Thema is a rare word for a theme or topic of discussion.

clue.text: What one's looking for in antique store

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A collector browses an antique shop for something specific.
explanation.definitionFit: A quest is a search, so what one is looking for is its object, by extension.

clue.text: Boundary trees

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., a fortified frontier of the Roman Empire
second meaning: citrus or linden trees

explanation.surface: Trees planted along a boundary line.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is a Latin word (plural limites) and is pronounced in two syllables.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman frontier was a limes, and lime trees in the plural are limes, so one spelling serves both.

clue.text: Hydrozoan, odious, not the first found swimming in the sea

indicators.note: swimming means moving freely about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
says the opening letter of the adjective is dropped

explanation.surface: An unpleasant jellyfish-like creature is found swimming in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A medusoid is the jellyfish-like stage of a hydrozoan, so it is one by example.

clue.text: Mouldings in warehouse, front to back

indicators.note: the opening letter moves round to the end of the word

explanation.surface: Mouldings stocked in a warehouse are moved from front to back.
explanation.definitionFit: A tore, or torus, is a large convex moulding at the base of a column.

clue.text: One practising turns in front of the author produces CV

indicators.note: places the first piece ahead of the word for the author
turns means flips round, so the practitioner word runs backwards

parts.note: someone who uses, as of a habit

explanation.surface: A practising performer turns up before the writer with a CV.
explanation.walkthrough: In American English, and here with the accent dropped, a résumé is a CV.
explanation.definitionFit: A résumé is the American name for a curriculum vitae, a summary of one's career.

clue.text: Mosque officer? Don't give —— for 'is supper!

wordplay.note: the blank is two cockney words with dropped h's, a pronoun and a cured meat, matching the 'is that follows

explanation.surface: A cockney warning not to give someone ham for supper.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h in 'is shows the blank is spoken the same way: 'im 'am. A Muslim cleric, fittingly, would not eat ham.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque, so he is one of its officers; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Ides possibly? Character ending life enters underworld

indicators.note: enters means goes inside, so that letter is put within the underworld

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god and realm of the underworld

indicators.note: the closing letter, or character, of the word for existence is used

explanation.surface: On the Ides of March a life ends and passes into the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: Ides looks like a scramble of the answer, but it is the definition: dies is Latin for day, and the Ides was a day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides was a fixed day in the Roman calendar, and dies is the Latin word for a day.

clue.text: Scots on top? Or, when England rallies, they're leading

indicators.note: leading means at the front, so the opening letters of the four preceding words are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A Scot asks whether England are winning when they rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Ower is the Scots form of over, which can mean above or on top.

clue.text: Pre-natal mishandled, in disorder, showing lack of respect

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase: the showing of a lack of respect

indicators.note: in says the jumbled letters go inside the word for disorder
mishandled means badly treated, so the letters of the first word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Maternity care badly handled and chaotic is treated as disrespect.
explanation.definitionFit: Malapertness is sauciness or impudence, an old word for cheeky disrespect.
